question: Did Jesus say, "Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up"?
summary: John 2:19-21 has Jesus straightforwardly speak this saying as a public pronouncement at the temple cleansing, and the narrator helpfully tells us he meant the temple of his body. Matthew 26:59-61 and Mark 14:57-58 report the saying being introduced at Jesus' trial only by *false witnesses* whose testimony was inadmissible because they couldn't even agree on the wording. One gospel has Jesus saying it on the record; two others say it was a slander invented by people trying to get him killed.

reconcile.connective: Harmonizers read the trial testimony as a garbled distortion of Jesus' real saying, which John 2:19-21 preserves accurately as a body-resurrection metaphor.

discrepancy.connective: Bart Ehrman presses the tension by noting that Mark's false witnesses report a saying strikingly close to what John attributes to Jesus verbatim, raising the question of which evangelist — or which tradition — has the more reliable version.

excerpts.attribution: John Gill, Exposition of the Entire Bible (1746-63)
excerpts.excerpt_text: in which they did injury, both to his words and sense: he did not say, "I am able to destroy the temple", but only said, "destroy this temple"; signifying neither his power, nor his will and inclination to it; but put it upon the Jews, and left it to them to do it: nor did he say one word about the temple of God, or as it is in Mar 14:58, "this temple that is made with hands"; the temple at Jerusalem, which was made by the hands of men, and devoted to the worship of God; but only "this temple", referring to his body, or human nature; in which he, the Son of God, dwelt, as in a temple
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Gill directly compares the false witnesses' version with Jesus' original words, itemising three specific distortions — thus directly engaging the question of whether the trial testimony contradicts the John 2 saying.
excerpts.source_note_text:
And said, this fellow said,.... Or saith, as De Dieu observes, the Syriac version of this place should be rendered; that is, he has not only said in times past, referring to Joh 2:19, but continues to say it, and glory in it:
I am able to destroy the temple of God, and to build it in three days; in which they did injury, both to his words and sense: he did not say, "I am able to destroy the temple", but only said, "destroy this temple"; signifying neither his power, nor his will and inclination to it; but put it upon the Jews, and left it to them to do it: nor did he say one word about the temple of God, or as it is in Mar 14:58, "this temple that is made with hands"; the temple at Jerusalem, which was made by the hands of men, and devoted to the worship of God; but only "this temple", referring to his body, or human nature; in which he, the Son of God, dwelt, as in a temple; nor did he say that he was able to "build" it in three days, but that he would "raise it up" in three days; intending the resurrection of his body by his own power, after it had been dead three days; and so they perverted his sense, as well as misquoted his words; applying that to the material temple at Jerusalem, what he spoke of the temple of his body, and of its resurrection from the dead, on the third day; designing hereby to fix a charge, both of sacrilege and sorcery upon him: of sacrilege, in having a design upon the temple of God to destroy it; and of sorcery, or familiarity with the devil, and having assistance from him, or knowledge of the magic art, that he could pretend in three days to rebuild a temple, which had been forty and six years in building; and was what could never be done, but by help of Beelzebub, the prince of devils, by whom it was insinuated he did all his miracles.
